clue.text: Interfering person's partial recall of howdy-do by subeditor

indicators.note: recall of says the hidden letters are read backwards
partial says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone half-remembers a greeting a subeditor once gave them.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of the definition stands for 'is': the interfering person is the answer. 'Partial' finds YDOBYSUB inside 'howdy-do by subeditor'; 'recall of' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A meddler who pokes into other people's affairs is the classic interfering person.

clue.text: Figure with pot or empty dish held by comic partner of Lou C

indicators.note: held by says the emptied dish sits inside the comedian's name

parts.note: Lou Costello's comedy partner was Bud Abbott, so with his surname cut to its initial, as Costello's is, he is Bud A

indicators.note: an empty dish has had its inside removed, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A comic double act with a pot or a bare dish as props.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lou C' abbreviates Costello, telling you to shorten his partner the same way: BUD A. The 'or' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Statues of the Buddha, especially the laughing kind, show a figure with a round pot belly.

clue.text: Man cooking up wild things kneads duff

indicators.note: duff is British slang for bad or useless, so the letters of the word before it are put wrong

explanation.surface: A cook makes a mess of kneading something wild in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: Maurice Sendak wrote and illustrated Where the Wild Things Are, so he 'cooked up' wild things. 'Duff' scrambles KNEADS.
explanation.definitionFit: The American author invented the Wild Things of his famous picture book.

clue.text: Diminutive singer brought up this, the lullaby's odd parts

indicators.note: brought up in a down clue means the letters are read from the bottom upwards, so backwards
odd parts asks for the first, third, fifth letters and so on from the words that follow

explanation.surface: A small singer was raised on this very lullaby.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd letters of 'this, the lullaby' give TITEULB; 'brought up' turns them round in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: This small garden songbird is a tiny member of the tit family, so a little singer.

clue.text: Churchmen wanting a heavy vehicle reduced time to break down

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the word a is taken out

parts.note: deacons are ordained ministers in the church

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a truck is a heavy goods vehicle

explanation.surface: Clergy without a lorry take time to come apart.
explanation.definitionFit: To analyse something by taking it apart into its pieces is to break it down, especially a text.

clue.text: Minor eminence in report of brave hardship when losing out

indicators.note: report of says the words are heard rather than written, so the entry sounds like them

parts.note: to brave hardship is to tough it out; losing the word out leaves tough it

explanation.surface: A minor dignitary is said to have borne hardship until he lost his post.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop 'out' from TOUGH IT OUT; said aloud, TOUGH IT gives the entry. 'Minor eminence' is a little hillock, not a junior VIP.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuffet is a small mound or hummock, a little raised spot of ground, as in Little Miss Muffet.

clue.text: Big Country music producer (for Strummer) welcoming The Fall?

indicators.note: welcoming means taking a guest in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a uke, short for ukulele, is an instrument you strum, so it produces music for a strummer
rain is what falls from the sky, a fall of water

explanation.surface: Rock bands everywhere: Big Country, Joe Strummer of the Clash, and The Fall, all in one picture.
explanation.walkthrough: Big Country and The Fall were British bands and Joe Strummer led the Clash, but here Strummer is just someone strumming.
explanation.definitionFit: Ukraine is the largest nation lying wholly within Europe, so a big country.

clue.text: Grass mostly found among fine speed and crack

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads

indicators.note: found among says one piece is set inside the others

parts.note: to race is to speed

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, so its last letter goes

parts.note: turf is grass and the soil it grows in

explanation.surface: A groundsman finds grass fine, but racing leaves cracks in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A fracture is a break or split, which is what a crack is.

clue.text: Main man brother's got in pocket

indicators.note: got in means put inside, so these pieces go into the small word

parts.note: pocket as an adjective means very small, as in a pocket edition
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: The main man's brother has stuffed something in his pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like an adjective but is the old word for the open sea. The 's is 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a poetic word for the sea, and the briny is its jokey everyday name.

clue.text: Accuse a person about breaking dipstick

indicators.note: breaking means splitting the other word open and sitting in the gap

parts.note: dipstick is slang for a stupid person, a dunce

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: one can mean a person, as in one should

explanation.surface: Someone is accused of breaking the oil dipstick in a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dipstick' looks like the car's oil gauge but is slang for an idiot; 'about' turns the person round before it breaks in.
explanation.definitionFit: To denounce someone is to accuse them publicly or inform against them.

clue.text: Maybe pomade, when included in Continental cut

indicators.note: included in says this piece sits inside the shortened word
cut means the final letter is lopped off

parts.note: a Greek is a Continental, a person from mainland Europe
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A European barber includes some pomade with every haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Continental' here means a person from mainland Europe; 'Maybe' warns that pomade is just one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomade is a scented oil or ointment for the hair, one example of a greasy substance.

clue.text: Score changed by half after try gets cheer

indicators.note: after says the halved number comes after the court word

parts.note: to hear a case in court is to try it
a score is twenty, so halving it gives ten

explanation.surface: A rugby score is changed after a try, and the crowd cheers.
explanation.walkthrough: In the surface 'try' is rugby; here it is a judge trying a case.
explanation.definitionFit: To hearten someone is to encourage them and lift their spirits, which is to cheer them.

clue.text: One with patchy employment who shirks, switching tons to learner

indicators.note: switching one letter for another means a T is replaced by an L

parts.note: a quitter is someone who gives up and shirks the job
L stands for learner, as on British L-plates

explanation.surface: A shirker in casual work, switching from heavy tonnage to training.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'patchy employment' is a pun: the quilter's work is sewing patches together, not an unsteady job.
explanation.definitionFit: A quilter sews pieces of fabric into patchwork, so the work is literally patchy.

clue.text: Multiple birth results as doctor finished cancelled services

parts.note: qua is Latin for as, in the capacity of
up means finished, as in 'time is up'
in tennis a let is a serve that is cancelled and replayed

explanation.surface: A doctor reports birth results after his surgery appointments were cancelled.
explanation.definitionFit: Four babies born at one birth are a multiple birth, and the four children are its result.

clue.text: Few planes can contain this wild deer, not holding stag back

indicators.note: holding means the scrambled letters wrap round the turned word
wild means out of control, so the letters before it run free into a new order
back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a hart is a male deer, a stag

explanation.surface: A wild deer runs loose but has no stag with it, while few planes could hold it.
explanation.walkthrough: The planes are flat faces of a solid, not aircraft; 'wild' scrambles 'deer, not' around the stag turned by 'back'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pyramid with a triangular base has just four flat faces, the fewest any solid can have, so few planes enclose it.

clue.text: Singular women excited Sappho where trades could be arranged

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the poet's name is jumbled

explanation.surface: A unique group of women get excited by the poet Sappho.
explanation.definitionFit: A swap shop is a place or event where people exchange goods instead of buying them.

clue.text: Start to get annoyed about content of suit's bonus payment

indicators.note: start to means the opening letter of the next word
about says the irritable word goes round the inner letters

parts.note: ratty is informal British for irritable or annoyed

indicators.note: content of means the inner letters, with the outer ones removed

explanation.surface: A man gets annoyed when his suit's contents reveal a bonus.
explanation.walkthrough: RATTY is British slang for irritable; 'about' wraps it round the inside of 'suit', between its two Ts.
explanation.definitionFit: A gratuity is a tip or extra payment given on top of what is owed, so a bonus.

clue.text: Perhaps a hundred and one spelt out simple filled grids

definitions.text: Perhaps a hundred and one spelt out
definitions.meaning: a hundred and one are both square numbers, ten times ten and one times one, and spelt out they are squares written in words
puzzles where words fill a small grid reading the same across and down

explanation.surface: A hundred and one simple crossword grids, spelt out in full.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is a cryptic pun: HUNDRED and ONE are squares written as words.
explanation.definitionFit: These are grids of letters where each row and its matching column hold the same word, the simplest kind of filled puzzle.

clue.text: Show excellence in leg meat to dine on

parts.note: shin is a cut of beef from the lower leg
to dine on something is to eat it

explanation.surface: A chef shows off by serving leg of meat for dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: To shine at something is to excel at it, to show talent there.

clue.text: Rest they use when shattered

indicators.note: when shattered means broken into pieces, so the letters of the words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: People use rest when they are exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shattered' is British slang for exhausted, which makes the surface read naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: Shut-eye is an informal word for sleep, a period of rest.

clue.text: Sceptical comment on enthusiasm for bullying

parts.note: ha is an exclamation of scorn or disbelief
zing means energy or zest

explanation.surface: A cynic's remark about someone's keenness for bullying.
explanation.definitionFit: Hazing is the American term for humiliating initiation rituals, a form of bullying.

clue.text: Valet and his master ignoring days before court: that's where I was a fool

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving those letters out of the names

parts.note: P. G. Wodehouse's valet Jeeves and his master Bertie Wooster

indicators.note: before says the days word comes ahead of the court word

parts.note: eves are the days before festivals
to woo is to court

explanation.surface: Bertie Wooster, the narrator 'I', recalls fooling about before court with his valet.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeeves and Wooster lose EVES then WOO. The 'I' is Bertie, Wodehouse's narrator and a famous fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A jester was the court entertainer, the king's professional fool.

clue.text: Well-rehearsed comedian who provides support nationally?

parts.note: pat means glib or rehearsed, as in a pat answer
a riot is someone hilariously funny

explanation.surface: A comedian with a polished act supports a national cause.
explanation.definitionFit: A patriot loves and backs their country, so supports it nationally.

clue.text: Feathers stop having old lady in ecstasy

indicators.note: having ... in means holding something inside
having ... in means holding something inside

parts.note: a plug stops a hole
ma is a name for one's mother, the old lady
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A man stops having his old lady around because of her ecstasy habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumage is a bird's covering of feathers.

clue.text: The girl keeps one of a pair in heels, assuming she's too young to have calves

definitions.text: she's too young to have calves

indicators.note: keeps means holding something inside

parts.note: her refers to a girl

parts.words: one of a pair in heels
parts.note: heels has two of the letter E, so one of the pair is E
if means assuming, as in 'if so'

explanation.surface: A girl in high heels thinks she's too young to show off her calves.
explanation.walkthrough: The calves are baby cows, not legs, so the girl in heels is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: A heifer is a young cow that has not yet had a calf.

clue.text: Left in crumbling (dire, etc) situation?

indicators.note: in says the left letter goes inside the scrambled letters
crumbling means falling apart, so the letters in brackets are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned in a dire, crumbling place.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines it while the parts build it; 'situation?' just completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A derelict building has been abandoned and left to fall into ruin.

clue.text: Drug trifle over sports energy drinks

indicators.note: drinks means taking something inside

parts.note: PE is physical education, sports in school
E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a toy is a trifle, something played with

explanation.surface: A trifle soaked in sports energy drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Peyote is a cactus that is the source of mescaline, a hallucinogenic drug.

clue.text: Austrian psychiatrist drops distributor

definitions.meaning: Hans ..., the Austrian doctor who described a form of autism
a sprinkler of holy water drops in church, from Latin aspergere, to sprinkle

explanation.surface: An Austrian psychiatrist falls from favour as distributor.
explanation.definitionFit: The doctor's surname is also a rare word for one who sprinkles holy water.
